name: Carlos Salvador Bilardo
scopeNote: Counted: Estudiantes de La Plata (1982 Metropolitano title, won 14 Feb 1983; exact appointment/departure days not found, 1982-01-01 and 1983-02-24 are approximate, sources only give years) and Argentina national team (appointment officialised about 10 days after 14 Feb 1983 per El Gráfico, first squad list 16 Mar 1983, debut 12 May 1983; last match the 1990 World Cup final on 8 Jul 1990). Style term used by sources: 'Bilardismo' / 'anti-fútbol' (from Zubeldía), pragmatic, with 3-5-2 (3 centre-backs: libero plus two man-markers) introduced 1984 and used from the 1986 quarter-final. The popular label '3-5-2 inventor' is Bilardo's own claim; TFT calls it likely an embellishment. In 1986 he started with a 4-4-2 (SI/Wilson). Marking: sources describe man-markers (Cuciuffo, Ruggeri) on forwards, no source found stating a general zonal or man-to-man policy. Excluded spells have year-only dates because sources give no days. Quotes with an undated origin carry the article date as earliest appearance found. Excluded: earlier Estudiantes (1971, 1973-76), Deportivo Cali (1976-78, Libertadores runner-up 1978: recognisable but dates unverified and no tactical coverage found), San Lorenzo 1979, Colombia 1979-81, Sevilla, Boca, Guatemala, Libya, Estudiantes 2003-04 (no major titles or tactical coverage within budget).
openQuestions: Exact start and end days of the Estudiantes 1981/82-83 spell not found (BeSoccer says 1981-1983, Wikipedia 1982-1983).
Argentina appointment: El Gráfico says officialised ~24 Feb 1983; Topmercato says March 1983.
No primary source found for the 3-5-2 quote of 1984; Wilson/SI gives it without citation.
Maradona's debut under Bilardo: El Gráfico says May 1985 (9 May v Paraguay); other sources cite earlier appearances, to confirm.
1990 team tactics (Italia 90) have only lineup and context evidence; no tactical analysis page was read.
Zonal vs man-marking: only match-specific man-markers (Cuciuffo, Ruggeri) are verified; Estudiantes 1982 marking not covered.
Excluded Deportivo Cali 1976-78 (Libertadores final 1978) could merit a counted spell; dates differ between sources (1976, 1977).

sources.title: Maradona the coach can learn from experience of Maradona the player (Jonathan Wilson)
sources.evidence: Initially, Bilardo had used a 4-4-2, before switching to deploy Jose Luis Cuciuffo as a man-marker, picking up Giuseppe Calderisi in the second game against Italy. With Jorge Luis Brown operating as a libero, that effectively left Oscar Garre to push forward from left back to join the midfield, with Maradona as an attacking central midfielder.

sources.title: Maradona the coach can learn from experience of Maradona the player (Jonathan Wilson)
sources.evidence: In Brown, he had an uncomplicated defensive libero. In front of him were the two markers, Oscar Ruggeri and Cuciuffo, who picked up the opposing center forwards. Sergio Batista operated in front of them as a ball-winner, with Julio Olarticoechea -- preferred to the more defensively minded Garre -- and Ricardo Giusti wide.

sources.title: Maradona the coach can learn from experience of Maradona the player (Jonathan Wilson)
